config.text: Own your website outright — files and all. First year of hosting free with a custom build.

config.headline: You should own your website. Not rent it.
config.body: Most website builders keep your site on their platform. Stop paying and it is gone — and there is nothing to take with you. We build yours from standard parts, hand you the whole thing, and you can move it anywhere, any time. Or stay with us. Your call.

media.alt: Diagram of a plate holding a grid of tiles

items.title: It is built from parts
items.body: Think Lego. A heading, a gallery, a menu, a contact form — each is a separate piece. We use the pieces your business actually needs and leave the rest in the box.

items.title: The parts fit together
items.body: Take one out and the rest still stand. Add one next year without rebuilding what is already there, and nothing you add breaks something you already had.

items.title: And you keep the box
items.body: The pieces are yours. Move them to another host, hand them to another designer, or stay with us — it is the same set of parts either way.

items.title: Build it here, in the browser
items.body: Open the builder, pick your parts, put them in order, and watch the result as you go. Nothing to install, no account, and no cost.

items.title: Download it and do it yourself
items.body: Take the files and work on them in whatever you already use. There is nothing to install and nothing to compile.

items.title: Let an AI build it for you
items.body: Point an AI coding assistant at the project and describe what you want. It builds to a fixed set of rules, so it does not wander off.

items.title: Or pay us to do the lot
items.body: $500 once, we build the whole thing, and we hand you the finished files. The first year of hosting is on us.

items.question: I am not technical. Is that a problem?
items.answer: No. If we build it, you get one simple screen for changing words, colours and photos — no code, and nothing you can break. If you would rather do it yourself, that is free, and we will point you at the two or three things worth knowing.

items.question: Why would I pay monthly if I own the site?
items.answer: You do not have to. Hosting and management is optional. It covers keeping the site online, updates, and a person to call when something needs changing. Take the files somewhere else and stop paying whenever you like.

items.question: How is this different from Wix or Squarespace?
items.answer: With those, your site lives inside their platform — that is what the monthly fee is renting. Here it is a set of files you hold. It is also why this page appears in a fraction of a second: there is no platform running behind it.

items.question: What happens if I want to leave?
items.answer: You take the files and go. Any host will run them. We would rather earn the $79 a month than hold your website hostage for it.

items.question: Will a new website actually get me customers?
items.answer: Usually not on its own. If you are a local business, most of your visitors come from Google Maps and your Google Business Profile, not from the website. A good site supports that — it repeats your address and hours exactly, and catches the searches Maps cannot serve. If your profile is out of date, fixing that may matter more than the site, and we will tell you so on the call.

config.title: What is included, and what is not

items.question: What exactly do I get for the $500?
items.answer: A complete site: your pages, your words, your photos, built and tested on a phone and on a desktop. You get the finished files, permanently. The first year of hosting and management is included, so the first thing you pay after that is optional.

items.question: Is the monthly payment mandatory?
items.answer: No. Hosting and management is a service, not a lock. Take the files to another host and stop paying whenever you like — the site keeps working. That is the difference between this and a site builder.

items.question: Do you take a cut of my sales?
items.answer: No. There is no checkout on your site at launch — we link out to wherever you already sell, and you keep your existing payment setup and your own customer relationships.

items.question: Do you do marketing as well?
items.answer: Not as part of the monthly. The site is built to be found: it repeats your address and opening hours exactly, and it carries the machine-readable details search engines read. Marketing and SEO is a separate service if you want it.

items.question: What if I need changes later?
items.answer: Small ones you can make yourself from a simple admin screen — words, colours, photos, at no cost. Bigger changes are what the monthly covers, and anything beyond that we will quote.

items.question: Can I see it before I commit?
items.answer: Yes. The builder on this site lets you assemble a page and read it live without an account or a card. It is the same engine we would use to build yours.

config.headline: Tell us what you need
config.body: Fifteen minutes is enough to say whether a new site is what you need, and what it would cost. No pitch, and no obligation.

config.headline: For the people who will build it
config.body: S.I.T.E.S is a specification, not a library. Nothing to install, nothing to compile, and no dependency to keep current. These pages are the contracts: what a compliant site is, how the grid works, how a site is authored, and how to assemble one by hand.

items.title: A specification, not a dependency
items.body: The rules a compliant site follows — ten of them, and this site obeys every one. Nothing to upgrade, because there is nothing to install.

items.title: A grid with two modes
items.body: An automatic auto-fit grid for ordinary pages, and a configured twelve-column grid when a layout has to be exact. A container query per tile handles every screen without a breakpoint.

items.title: One content file
items.body: Copy, theme, navigation and images live in one JSON document. The markup owns structure; the file owns the words, and the admin edits it.

items.title: Tiles that compose
items.body: Every part declares the fields it accepts, so the admin, the builder and the linter all read one declaration instead of three lists that drift.

items.title: Quickstart — build one by hand
items.body: Copy a starter page, paste tiles into it, put your words in the content file. A text editor and a browser are the whole toolchain.

items.title: The grid
items.body: How the two layout modes work, why there are no breakpoints, and how a tile reflows by its own width rather than the window width.

items.title: The standard

items.title: The blueprint format

config.headline: The repository is the documentation

config.tagline: Built with the framework it documents.

config.headline: Build it by hand
config.body:
No AI, no build step. Copy a starter page, paste tiles into it, put your words in
a content file. A text editor and a browser are the whole toolchain.

items.title: 1 · Copy the starter
items.body: Take templates/plate.html, rename it index.html. It already has the plate, the nav and the footer.

items.title: 2 · Paste a tile
items.body: Pick a tile from the kit, paste its markup inside <main>.

items.title: 3 · Add the words
items.body: Put the matching entry in content.json — same id as the markup's data-tile-id.

items.title: 4 · Refresh
items.body: That is the whole cycle. Change a word in the JSON and watch it move.

items.title: You need
items.body: A text editor, a browser, and Python (or any static server) to preview locally. Some HTML and CSS familiarity helps.

items.title: You do not need
items.body: Node, npm, a bundler, a framework, a build pipeline, or a hosting account to start.

items.title: Coming from a site builder?
items.body: If you can drag a section onto a page, you can paste one. The mental model is three ideas — see the kit's primer.

config.headline: The two files that teach it
config.body: plate.html is the starter; TILE-KIT.md holds every tile's markup and its content entry, ready to copy.

config.headline: Ship it anywhere
config.body: Copy the folder plus the framework files, upload to Firebase Hosting, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Netlify or IPFS. Nothing to build.

config.headline: The standard
config.body:
S.I.T.E.S is a specification, not a library. These are the rules a compliant site
follows — everything on this site obeys them.

items.title: No build step
items.body: Plain .html, .css and .js. No bundler, no package manager, nothing to compile — the source is the site.

items.title: Tokens, never literals
items.body: Every colour, space, radius and shadow comes from a CSS custom property. That is what makes re-theming instant.

items.title: Breakpoint-free layout
items.body: One auto-fit grid handles the macro layout; container queries let a tile adapt to its own width, not the window.

items.title: Copy is data
items.body: Editable words live in the content file and bind into slots. The HTML owns structure only.

items.title: Progressive by default
items.body: The page reads correctly with JavaScript disabled; behaviour is layered on top.

items.title: Services, not vendors
items.body: Forms, maps, payments and AI are swappable adapters selected by configuration — never hard-coded into a tile.

config.title: The whole responsive system

items.title: L1 Structural
items.body: The plate and tiles model, with tiles built to the naming and data contract.

items.title: L2 Presentation
items.body: Full tokenization, breakpoint-free layout, accessible and progressive.

items.title: L3 Content-managed
items.body: Copy externalised to a schema-valid content file, editable from the admin.

items.title: L4 Managed and sovereign
items.body: L3 plus a portable storage adapter and no third-party trackers. This site targets L4.

items.question: Do I have to use the content file?
items.answer: No. For a small static page you can write the copy straight into the HTML. The moment someone else needs to edit it, move the words into the content file.

items.question: Can I add my own CSS?
items.answer: Yes — in your own stylesheet, using the tokens. Never hardcode colours, or re-theming stops working.

items.question: Is there a JavaScript framework?
items.answer: No, and that is the point. Tiles register their own behaviour through SITES.register and stay scoped to their element.

config.headline: Go deeper
config.body: The repository holds the architecture, module spec, content model, theme engine, assets and integration specs.

config.headline: Write it as a blueprint
config.body:
A site can be authored as one Markdown file — front matter for the site, theme and
nav, then one section per tile. Compile it to content.json, then build the pages.

config.title: Front matter
config.code:
---
site:
name: My site
baseUrl: https://example.com
theme:
colors: { background: "#F7F8FA", primary: "#1B3A5C", accent: "#2F6FED" }
dark:   { background: "#0B0F17", text: "#E7ECF3" }
nav:
- Home: /
- Services: /services.html
integrations:
forms: formspree
---

config.title: One section per tile
config.code:
path: /

description: Opening band.
id: home-hero
headline: Your headline
body: |
A sentence that explains what this is.
actions:
- label: Get started
href: /contact
style: gold

items.title: Gather
items.body: Fill the intake form — business, brand, sitemap, per-tile copy, integrations.

items.title: Author
items.body: Write the blueprint. Humans and AI agents both produce this format, so either can pick up the other's work.

items.title: Compile
items.body: tools/blueprint.mjs emits content.json and warns about unknown tiles or unregistered fields.

items.title: Compose
items.body: Paste the tile markup into a page. Structure and CSS are fixed; the words come from the file.

config.headline: One command
config.body: The compiler is build-time only — the delivered site stays dependency-free. It validates tile types and field names against the tile registry, so a typo becomes a warning rather than a broken page.

items.question: Is the blueprint required?
items.answer: No. It is a convenience for authoring and for AI collaboration. You can edit content.json directly, or edit the copy in the admin.

items.question: Can an AI write the blueprint?
items.answer: Yes — that is the intended division of labour. The AI drafts the blueprint, the compiler produces the site, the owner maintains the copy in the admin.

config.headline: The grid
config.body:
Two ways to lay tiles out. The automatic grid fits as many columns as it can —
zero configuration. The configured grid gives you 12 columns on wide containers
and 6 on narrow ones, and every tile declares its own width.

items.title: Automatic — .sites-grid
items.body: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(300px, 1fr)). No breakpoints, no column maths. Perfect for rows of equal cards.

items.title: Configured — .sites-grid--cols
items.body: A 12-column grid (6 when narrow) where each tile says how wide it is with data-span. For deliberate layouts.

config.code:

two thirds

config.headline: data-span="4"
config.body: A third of the wide grid. On the narrow tier this is full width.

config.headline: data-span="4"
config.body: Three of these fill one deliberate row.

config.headline: data-span="4"
config.body: Change one number and the whole row rearranges.

config.headline: data-span="8"
config.body: Two thirds. Pair an 8 with a 4 for an asymmetric row.

config.headline: data-span="4"
config.body: The narrow companion to the 8 above.

config.headline: narrow 1
config.body: data-span-sm="2" — three across even on a phone.

config.headline: narrow 2
config.body: The same tile also declares data-span="4" for the wide tier.

config.headline: narrow 3
config.body: Two numbers, two screen sizes, no media queries in your code.

items.title: What you see below
items.body: Real tiles with data-span, not a picture. Resize the window and watch the tiers switch.

items.title: data-span="4"
items.body: Three across on the wide tier. Any whole number from 1 to 12.

items.title: data-span="8"
items.body: Two thirds — pair it with a 4 for a classic asymmetric row.

items.title: data-span-sm="2"
items.body: Three across on the narrow tier too (spans of the 6-column narrow grid).

items.title: no data-span
items.body: Full width, one tile per row. The safe default.

items.title: .sites-grid--start
items.body: Tiles size to their own content instead of stretching to equal heights.

items.title: .tile--center
items.body: Centres a tile's text and its button row.

items.title: .tile--end
items.body: Pushes text and buttons to the end (right in a left-to-right language).

items.title: bottom-aligned buttons
items.body: Buttons in cards, pricing tiers and products sit on the row baseline automatically, however much copy the neighbours carry.

config.headline: Configure it, or leave it alone
config.body: Most sites never need data-span. Reach for the configured grid when a row should be deliberately uneven.
